Chapter 156 0153: First, Invest a Sum with the Royalties

Chen Guiliang kept dragging things out, unwilling to engage in substantive negotiations, which led to Fu Jixun flying back to Shanghai, leaving only an investment manager to keep an eye on things.

Upon receiving Chen Guiliang's call, Fu Jixun did not reply immediately.

He had to contact Silicon Valley first and study Facebook's financing situation in detail!

At this time, DFJ was still relatively cautious about investing in China.

It wasn't until web 2.0 exploded in popularity the following year that Silicon Valley would send over more money to specifically establish a DFJ DragonFund China. At that point, the DFJ partners would be waving wads of cash, looking for internet companies all over China to throw money at.

As for IDG's Lin Dongliang, he also needed to understand the details of Facebook's financing first before he could slowly discuss the Xiaonei investment with Chen Guiliang.

Evening.

Chen Guiliang carried a bucket downstairs. Inside were his clothes to be washed and his toiletries. He headed to the public bathhouse with Guo Feng, Min Wenyu, and Jiang Junlai.

"Yo, CEO Chen, washing your own clothes again!"

Before they even arrived, they ran into a few acquaintances who joked with Chen Guiliang with a grin.

Chen Guiliang said boastfully, "When my company goes public, I'll hire a dedicated bath secretary to go to the public bathhouse for me."

"Haha, if it's a female secretary, she'll have to go to the women's bathhouse," someone else laughed.

Outside the public bathhouse, students were queuing.

The four of them, Chen Guiliang and his friends, placed their buckets and washbasins at the back of the line, then squatted to the side to chat.

A lively conversation was already going on there.

Soon, another boy joined in and said mysteriously, "News is out about the one who jumped from the Second Science Building yesterday. His surname is Feng, a PhD student in mathematics who was about to graduate!"

"Holy crap, a PhD student about to graduate jumped too?"

"Maybe his thesis couldn't pass."

"Who knows."

"Why does everyone choose the Second Science Building? The girl from the Chinese department who jumped last month was there too."

"Could it be haunted? A ghost messes with your head and you jump."

Chen Guiliang felt uneasy listening to this. Since he had enrolled, three people had already jumped at Peking University.

And it wasn't just Peking University. Last year, 10 students from major universities in Beijing had jumped, and this year, the number would even surge to 19. This sparked widespread public debate, and the Ministry of Education even got involved, requiring universities to strengthen students' psychological education.

In a few more days, another one from Peking University would jump, though not on campus. He would jump at Chengdu's Shuangliu Airport.

"Chen Guiliang!" a student suddenly called out.

Chen Guiliang turned his head. "What's up?"

That student asked, "The girl who jumped last month, was her suicide note written in a blog post on Xiaonei? Why can't I see it anymore?"

Chen Guiliang nodded. "Her blog post wasn't deleted, just hidden. Her family can see it by logging into her account. The password for that account has been reset and given to her family to manage."

"Sigh, why was it necessary? So young," that student said with great regret.

His phone rang, and Chen Guiliang ran under a tree to answer it.

"I've arrived in Beijing. Just checked into my hotel," Tao Chenggang said.

Chen Guiliang said, "Come directly to the Peking University Science Park tomorrow. Remember to call me a few minutes beforehand."

"Alright, we'll talk in person tomorrow," Tao Chenggang said.

Tao Chenggang had brought the share purchase agreement with him.

The first quarter's royalties for *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* had arrived half a month ago, amounting to over 1,563,000 yuan (after tax).

This was calculated at a 15% royalty rate. Once sales exceeded 500,000 copies, the rate would increase by 1% for every additional 100,000 copies, up to a maximum of 20%.

The extra money from the tiered calculation would be paid out in future settlements.

In addition, there was a reduction policy for personal income tax on royalties, which brought the final tax rate down to 11.2%.

Chen Guiliang had received a 100,000 yuan advance last year, which naturally had to be deducted, so he actually received a little over 1.46 million.

Of this amount, he planned to invest 400,000 yuan in Tao Chenggang's game company in his own name to help Tao Chenggang with his pressing needs.

Two hundred thousand of it was his own investment, and the other two hundred thousand would be counted as Bian Guanyue's. It wasn't a large stake and would be diluted in the future, but it would be enough to ensure Bian Guanyue would be financially secure, and it wouldn't cause any conflicts in company management.

After the venture capital funds arrived, he would continue to invest in Tao Chenggang's company under the name of Bytedance.

As long as this free-to-play game wasn't managed too poorly, it was sure to make big money.

After finishing their showers, on the way back to the dorm, Chen Guiliang called Bian Guanyue. "Take tomorrow off and come to the Peking University Science Park."

"Is it something urgent?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Chen Guiliang chuckled. "Didn't you lend me a few hundred thousand? I'm helping you invest two hundred thousand of it into a company. It's sure to be a good earner in the future."

"There's no need. Just pay me back when you have the money," Bian Guanyue said.

Chen Guiliang said, "Be good. Listen to me."

Bian Guanyue thought for a moment. "Alright, then. What time tomorrow?"

"Set off in the morning," Chen Guiliang said.

"Okay," Bian Guanyue replied.

After talking business, they chatted idly until he returned to dorm room 404.

Min Wenyu said to Guo Feng, "Madman Guo, look at Chen Guiliang, a winner in both love and his career. Why don't you go after your senior?"

"No time," Guo Feng said. "Actually, I do text her occasionally. She used to often not reply, but now she replies every time. I've analyzed it carefully. My behavior before was too abrupt, making her not know how to interact with me. Now that we don't see each other as much, our relationship has actually gotten better."

Jiang Junlai asked, "Could it be because you've become a company shareholder, and the company is still growing, that she's started to see you in a new light?"

"How vulgar!"

Guo Feng said with contempt.

Deng Chen from the room across the hall stood in the corridor and roared, "Need players for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*!"

"Coming!"

Jiang Junlai immediately ran out.

It wasn't just him; two other rooms next door also responded.

Although an online version of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* had been released, many students still didn't own a computer.

Besides, playing face-to-face had its own unique charm.

Senior Min didn't go to the room across the hall. He was borrowing Chen Guiliang's computer, constantly switching accounts to harvest and steal crops.

"Damn it, I take one shower and come back to find several accounts have been raided down to the bare minimum," Senior Min cursed.

"Resolutely refuse to top up!" Min Wenyu's attitude was firm.

Chen Guiliang tempted him, "I'll lend you money to top up, and you can pay me back whenever."

"Get lost, get lost! Don't drag me into this!" Senior Min resisted the temptation.

Chen Guiliang burst out laughing.

This was a matter of principle. Senior Min would rather treat him to barbecue than ever spend money on a game. He wouldn't even accept a VIP membership if Chen Guiliang offered it.

After replanting his crops, Min Wenyu said, "This summer vacation, I'm going to volunteer as a teacher. You, Mr. Capitalist, want to show some love for the children in the mountains?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Help me buy some popular science books to donate to the mountain schools, like *A Hundred Thousand Whys* and *Five Thousand Years Up and Down*."

"So you do have some conscience left, not completely corrupted by capital," Min Wenyu said with a laugh.

Guo Feng, who had been lying on his bed resting, said, "Help me donate some sports equipment, like basketballs, soccer balls, badminton rackets, and so on."

Chen Guiliang added another sentence, "If there are any students who are particularly diligent and studious but whose families are in real difficulty, help me record their information."

Min Wenyu was a bit surprised and took a serious look at Chen Guiliang. "Alright."

The next day.

Chen Guiliang arrived at the Peking University Science Park and found Wang Kai to borrow a meeting room temporarily. "Mr. Wang, why is there construction going on over there again?"

Wang Kai explained with a smile, "They're building the incubator building over there. It's only five stories, a top-tier design. Once it's finished, the startups will move over there, and this current building will be rented exclusively to mature enterprises."

"Are there any vacant office spaces in this building now?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Wang Kai said, "Fangzheng and Qingniao are moving in soon. Their renovations are already complete. Other floors are also being occupied by companies one after another. After you receive your investment, how many employees are you planning to expand to?"
